title: Best customers
description:
Customers and orders are separate lists (the records are already defined for you). Write `public static class Sales` with:

```csharp
public static List<(string Name, decimal Total)> Totals(IEnumerable<Customer> customers, IEnumerable<Order> orders)
```

It returns every customer with the sum of their orders, **including customers with no orders** (total 0), sorted by total (highest first) and then by name.
hints: `GroupJoin` keeps every customer and gives you the sequence of their orders, possibly empty, so `os.Sum(o => o.Total)` is 0 for them (lesson 8.01).
`OrderByDescending(t => t.Total).ThenBy(t => t.Name)` sorts by two keys.

support.Fixtures.cs:
public record Customer(int Id, string Name);
public record Order(int Id, int CustomerId, decimal Total);
